newsitem.title: FINLAND: NIINISTO SEES FINNISH EMU VOTE MAR-APR '98 - AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: NIINISTO SEES FINNISH EMU VOTE MAR-APR '98 - AGENCY.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Thursday that the Finnish parliament's vote on EMU membership was likely to take place in March-April 1998, the Finnish news agency STT reported.
The government would give a report on EMU to parliament once it had become clear which countries could qualify for the single currency, STT quoted him as saying.

A special summit of European Union heads of state and government is due to decide in early May next year which countries will join the third stage of economic and monetary union in the first wave scheduled for start-up in 1999.
The government hoped that parliament's constitutional committee would rule already this spring on what kind of majority would be needed for the spring 1998 EMU vote, Niinisto said.
The committee could do that in connection with another government report on EMU due in parliament in May, he said.
STT quoted Niinisto as saying Finland would decide on EMU independently of Sweden, but it would be desirable that the two neighbours would come to the same conclusion.
For Finland, remaining outside EMU would bring big economic risks and be seen as an attempt to retain the possibility to devalue its currency, Niinisto said.
